classification.difficultyReason: Combine cyclic supplementary angles with each shape's angle properties; the trapezium proof requires comparing two supplementary relationships to establish equal base angles.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Prove that a cyclic parallelogram is a rectangle.

spec.description: Unlabelled horizontal rectangle inscribed in a circle. Decorative cyan fill omitted under house style.
spec.mathematics: All four vertices lie on the circle; opposite sides are parallel. No angle or parallel markers are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied figure remains visible; no solution labels or marks are added.

answer.short: Opposite angles are equal and supplementary, so each is $90^{\circ}$. Thus the parallelogram is a rectangle.
answer.worked:
Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal. Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary. For either opposite pair, let each angle be $x$.
$$\begin{align*}2x&=180^{\circ}\\x&=90^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
Both opposite pairs therefore consist of right angles. The parallelogram has four right angles, so it is a rectangle.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Prove that a cyclic trapezium has two pairs of equal angles.

spec.description: Unlabelled cyclic trapezium with a shorter horizontal upper base and longer horizontal lower base. Decorative cyan fill omitted.
spec.mathematics: Four vertices on one circle; upper and lower bases parallel. No supplied angle or side markers.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied outline is shown.

answer.short:
$\angle A=\angle B$ and $\angle C=\angle D$, where $AB\parallel CD$.

Compare supplementary opposite angles with co-interior angles on the parallel bases.
answer.worked:
Label the vertices $A,B,C,D$ consecutively, with $AB\parallel CD$. Cyclic opposite angles and co-interior angles give
$$\begin{align*}\angle A+\angle C&=180^{\circ}\\\angle A+\angle D&=180^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
Hence $\angle C=\angle D$. Also,
$$\begin{align*}\angle A+\angle D&=180^{\circ}\\\angle B+\angle D&=180^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
Hence $\angle A=\angle B$. Thus the trapezium has two pairs of equal angles.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Prove that a cyclic kite has a pair of right angles.

spec.description: Unlabelled cyclic kite with a horizontal symmetry axis. Decorative cyan fill omitted.
spec.mathematics: All vertices lie on the circle; the upper and lower vertices are symmetric about the line through the left and right vertices. No supplied equal-side or right-angle markers.
spec.answerVisibility: No right-angle marks or solution labels are shown.

answer.short: The equal opposite angles are supplementary, so each is $90^{\circ}$.
answer.worked:
A kite has a pair of equal opposite angles. Because the kite is cyclic, these angles are supplementary. Let each be $x$.
$$\begin{align*}2x&=180^{\circ}\\x&=90^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
Thus the kite has a pair of right angles.
